title: National Legal Services Authority - Legal Aid
section: Eligibility - Who is entitled to free legal services
text: The sections of the society as enlisted under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act are entitled for free legal services, they are: A member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; A victim of trafficking in human beings or begar as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution; A woman or a child; A mentally ill or otherwise disabled person; A person under circumstances of undeserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; or An industrial workman; or In custody...; or a person in receipt of annual income less than the amount mentioned in the following schedule (or any other higher amount as may be prescribed by the State Government), if the case is before a Court other than the Supreme Court. Is a woman irrespective of her income/financial status eligible for free legal aid? Yes, a woman is entitled for free legal aid irrespective of her income or financial status. A woman is eligible to apply for free legal aid by virtue of Section 12(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
plain_summary: NALSA lists the Section 12 categories that are entitled to free legal services: members of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, victims of trafficking or begar, a woman or a child, a mentally ill or otherwise disabled person, victims of mass disaster or similar undeserved want, industrial workmen, and persons in custody. A person whose annual income is below the prescribed ceiling is also covered. A woman is eligible regardless of income. The income ceiling is set by the State Government and differs between States and Union Territories.
applicability_note: The listed income ceiling is the one prescribed by the State Government or Union Territory, so it varies by place and can change. This passage states eligibility categories only; it does not decide whether a particular person qualifies.

title: National Legal Services Authority - Legal Aid
section: Claiming Free Legal Aid / Application Procedure
text: Where should I approach in order to seek free legal services/aid? Depending upon the territorial and subject matter jurisdiction of the case, an individual should approach the following appropriate authority: Taluk Legal Services Committee which is in the premises of the Court in that Taluk; or District Legal Services Authority which is in the premises of the District Court in the District Headquarters; or The concerned State Legal Services Authority...; The High Court Legal Services Committee...; or The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee for cases before the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Each District Legal Services Authority, High Court Legal Services Committee and State Legal Services Authority has a front office where an application can be moved. One can even access and apply on the online portal of NALSA (https://nalsa.gov.in/). How can I apply for free legal aid? You can apply for free legal aid either offline or online. You can fill up the ready-made form/application form that is available at your nearest Legal Services Authority and submit the same at either the Authority physically, or post the application to the Authority. You can even make an application in writing on a simple piece of paper... Another option is to send the application online i.e. by email to NALSA (at nalsa-dla@nic.in), or through the online application form available online at NALSA's website... It is also possible to make your application orally - a paralegal volunteer or an officer of the concerned Legal Services Authority will assist you in such cases.
plain_summary: Apply to the Legal Services Authority that covers the area and the court where the case is: the Taluk Legal Services Committee, District Legal Services Authority, State Legal Services Authority, High Court Legal Services Committee, or Supreme Court Legal Services Committee. Each has a front office, and applications can also be made online through the NALSA portal or a State Legal Services Authority website. An application can be made on the printed form, on plain paper with the required details, by email, or orally with help from staff or a paralegal volunteer.
applicability_note: The right office depends on where the case is and which court or tribunal it is before. Contact details and online application links are maintained by NALSA and the State Legal Services Authorities and may change.

title: National Legal Services Authority - Legal Aid
section: Legal Services - What free legal aid includes
text: Free legal aid is the provision of free legal services in civil and criminal matters for those economically weaker section of the society and marginalized people who cannot afford the services of a lawyer for the conduct of a case or a legal proceeding in any Court, Tribunal or Authority. These services are governed by Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 and headed by the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). Provision of free legal aid may include: Representation by an Advocate in legal proceedings. Payment of process fees, expenses of witnesses and all other charges payable or incurred in connection with any legal proceedings in appropriate cases; Preparation of pleadings, memo of appeal, paper book including printing and translation of documents in legal proceedings; Drafting of legal documents, special leave petition etc. Supply of certified copies of judgments, orders, notes of evidence and other documents in legal proceedings. Free Legal Services also include provision of aid and advice to the beneficiaries to access the benefits under the welfare statutes and schemes framed by the Central Government or the State Government... According to Section 2(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, "legal services" includes any service in the conduct of any case or other legal proceeding before any court or other authority or tribunal and the giving of advice on any legal matter.
plain_summary: Free legal aid covers civil and criminal matters for people who cannot afford a lawyer. Depending on the case it can include an advocate to represent the person, payment of process fees and witness expenses, preparation of pleadings and appeal papers, drafting of legal documents, and certified copies of judgments and evidence. Legal services also include advice on legal matters and help in accessing welfare schemes.
applicability_note: The list describes what free legal aid may include; the assistance actually provided depends on the case and the Legal Services Authority. It is not a guarantee of a particular service or outcome.

title: National Legal Services Authority - Frequently Asked Questions
section: FAQs 9 to 11 - Cost of legal services and helpline
text: Whether one needs to pay for legal services provided by Legal Services Institutions constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987? No. Legal services provided by the Legal Services Institutions are completely free of cost to the beneficiary. All costs involved are borne by the Legal Services Institutions. Does one have to pay any charge/fee for acquiring or submitting an application form for free legal aid? No, there is absolutely no charge for getting or submitting an application form for free legal aid. Are there any Helpline Services provided by NALSA for urgent legal assistance? Yes. One can directly contact on NALSA Helpline Toll-Free Number 15100 to seek urgent legal assistance.
plain_summary: Legal services from the Legal Services Institutions are free of cost to the beneficiary, and there is no charge for getting or submitting a legal aid application form. NALSA also runs a toll-free helpline, 15100, for urgent legal assistance.
applicability_note: The helpline number and office arrangements are administrative and may change; confirm them on the NALSA website. This passage does not cover private lawyers' fees.
